Listen to this article Share Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football, bringing the curtain down on a record-breaking 23-year career with Portugal, during which he scored 146 goals in 234 appearances. The 41-year-old five-time Ballon d’Or winner confirmed his decision in a social media statement on Thursday, saying he would hand back Portugal’s iconic number seven shirt after the November international break. “Today I finish my walk on the pitch with the national team. I leave with my head held high, with pride in the path I took, and with the awareness that I gave everything I had for Portugal,” Ronaldo said. The Al-Nassr forward described representing Portugal as the greatest achievement of his career, reflecting on the records, trophies and memories he accumulated over more than two decades with the national team. “The goals pass, the cups are in museums, and the records end up being beaten. But there is something that time can never erase: the place we occupy in people’s hearts. “I spent my life working to be the best player in the world. Today I realise that the greatest victory was to have deserved to represent the best country in the world,” he added. Ronaldo retires as the leading goalscorer in men’s international football and the most-capped male international player. He also captained Portugal to their first major international trophy at Euro 2016 and led the country to two UEFA Nations League titles, in 2019 and 2025. From his emergence at Manchester United to his record-breaking exploits with Real Madrid and Portugal, Ronaldo’s career has been defined by remarkable goals, individual honours and major trophies. Here are seven landmark moments that shaped the career of one of football’s greatest players. First Premier League title with Manchester United in 2007 Ronaldo’s breakthrough at Manchester United came during the 2006-07 season, when he scored 17 Premier League goals to help the club win its first league title in four years. After arriving from Sporting CP in 2003, the Portuguese winger had steadily developed into one of the most exciting young players in English football. His performances earned him both the Professional Footballers’ Association (PFA) Players’ Player of the Year and Young Player of the Year awards in 2007, underlining his emergence as a leading figure in the Premier League. He had also won the FA Cup in his first season at Old Trafford, scoring in the 3-0 final victory over Millwall in 2004. El Clásico winner seals Copa del Rey for Real Madrid in 2011 Ronaldo delivered a defining moment in his early Real Madrid career when he scored the winning goal against Barcelona in the 2011 Copa del Rey final. With the match level after 90 minutes, Ronaldo rose at the far post to power home a header from Ángel Di María’s cross in extra time, giving Real Madrid a 1-0 victory at the Mestalla Stadium. The goal secured his first major trophy with the Spanish club and was particularly significant because it came against their fierce rivals in a high-profile final. Leads Portugal to historic Euro 2016 title One of the defining achievements of Ronaldo’s international career came at Euro 2016, when Portugal won their first major international title. Portugal defeated hosts France 1-0 after extra time in the final in Paris, with Eder scoring the decisive goal. Ronaldo was forced off injured in the first half, leaving the pitch in tears, but remained involved from the touchline, encouraging his teammates and taking on an unofficial coaching role. He finished the tournament with three goals and three assists and was named in the team of the tournament. Ronaldo also became the all-time leading goalscorer in European Championship history, with 14 goals across the finals. Wins fifth Ballon d’Or in 2017 Ronaldo collected his fifth Ballon d’Or in 2017, drawing level with Lionel Messi’s record at the time. The award followed a remarkable 2016-17 season in which he helped Real Madrid win both the UEFA Champions League and La Liga. He scored twice in the Champions League final against Juventus in Cardiff, helping Real Madrid secure a 4-1 victory and become the first club to retain the trophy in the competition’s modern era. The individual honour further cemented his status among the defining players of his generation. First player to score 100 Champions League goals in 2017 Ronaldo made more history in April 2017 when he became the first player to score 100 goals in the UEFA Champions League. He reached the milestone with a hat-trick in Real Madrid’s 4-2 extra-time victory over Bayern Munich in the quarter-final second leg. His record-breaking achievement reflected his extraordinary consistency in Europe’s premier club competition, where he went on to establish himself as its all-time leading goalscorer. First player to win five Champions League titles in 2018 Ronaldo became the first player to win the Champions League five times in the modern era when Real Madrid defeated Liverpool 3-1 in the 2018 final in Kyiv. He had won his first title with Manchester United in 2008 before lifting the trophy with Real Madrid in 2014, 2016, 2017 and 2018. The three consecutive triumphs with Real Madrid from 2016 to 2018 represented one of the most remarkable periods of dominance in the competition’s history. Record 985 career goals for club and country Ronaldo’s remarkable scoring record is perhaps the most enduring feature of his career. According to the figures supplied, he has scored 985 goals in 1,343 senior appearances for club and country, leaving him 15 goals short of the historic 1,000-goal milestone. His 146 goals in 234 appearances for Portugal also make him the leading scorer in men’s international football and the most-capped male international player. Beyond the numbers, his career has been defined by longevity, consistency and success across England, Spain, Italy, Saudi Arabia and international football. As he brings his Portugal career to an end, Ronaldo leaves behind a legacy shaped by individual records, major trophies and moments that have influenced football for more than two decades.
